claims.text: The target material is a multicomponent high-entropy material initially in the solid state.
High-entropy materials contain multiple principal elements and have a vast compositional space.
The proposed intervention is to incorporate machine-learning algorithms into CALPHAD.
Machine-learning-enhanced CALPHAD will improve the accuracy of transition-temperature determination.
Machine-learning-enhanced CALPHAD will improve the accuracy of fusion-enthalpy determination.
Machine-learning-enhanced CALPHAD will improve the accuracy of fusion-entropy determination.
Machine-learning-enhanced CALPHAD will improve the accuracy of volume-change determination at the solid-to-fluid transition.
Machine-learning-enhanced CALPHAD will improve the accuracy of dense-fluid heat-capacity determination.
Machine-learning-enhanced CALPHAD will improve the efficiency of determining the listed solid-to-fluid thermodynamic properties.
Configurational entropy is a structural mediator between machine-learning-enhanced CALPHAD and the predicted thermodynamic outcomes.
Short-range ordering or clustering is a structural mediator between machine-learning-enhanced CALPHAD and the predicted thermodynamic outcomes.
Nanostructure phase instabilities and morphologies mediate the predicted thermodynamic outcomes.
Machine-learning algorithms can screen the vast compositional space of high-entropy materials efficiently.
Machine learning can identify optimal high-entropy-material compositions.
Machine learning can identify optimal processing conditions for high-entropy materials.
The selected optimal compositions and processing conditions will produce improved thermodynamic-property determination.
Machine-learning accuracy depends on the size and quality of the training dataset.
Machine-learning accuracy depends on the complexity of the high-entropy material system.
The hypothesis is limited to multiple-principal-element high-entropy materials near a high-temperature solid-to-fluid transition.
